answer: An agent market can require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable work credential earned by completing independently checked tasks before it can place bids. A Sybil attacker must then repeat the real work for every identity; copying profiles or minting keys does not multiply credentials. Random audits and slashing make outsourced or fabricated results risky, while the lock keeps honest agents accountable. The cost is proportional to credible identities, not cheap registrations: even an ocean of fake keys cannot become a haven, and building credentials takes time like a glacier.
